content: If you are using this medication to self-treat and your symptoms of acid-related issues persist or worsen after two weeks of use, or if you suspect you may have a serious medical condition, seek medical attention immediately. If you are taking this medication daily for more than two weeks, it may indicate an underlying medical issue that requires alternative treatment. If your doctor has prescribed this medication for conditions such as acidosis or to alkalinize your urine, the dosage will be determined based on your specific medical condition and response to treatment. To achieve the best results, take this medication regularly and exactly as directed. It is typically administered orally several times a day. To help you remember, take it at the same times each day. Common side effects may include nausea, bloating, or gas. If your doctor has recommended this medication, it is because they have determined that the benefits outweigh the potential risks of side effects. When taken with sodium bicarbonate, consuming large amounts of calcium from your diet, medications, or supplements can, in rare cases, lead to a serious condition known as milk-alkali syndrome. Consult your doctor or pharmacist about the safe use of calcium products while on this medication. Severe allergic reactions to this medication are rare. However, this is not an exhaustive list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for similar guidance. Before taking sodium bicarbonate, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other complications. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary, as it may exacerbate high blood pressure during pregnancy. Additionally, this medication may pass into breast milk. Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs, as well as herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication can reduce the effectiveness of certain drugs that require stomach acid to work, such as ampicillin, atazanavir, certain azole antifungals (e.g., ketoconazole, itraconazole), iron supplements, pazopanib, sucralfate, and others. If your doctor has advised you to take low-dose aspirin (81-162 milligrams daily) to prevent heart attack or stroke, continue taking it unless instructed otherwise. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. If you are taking large doses of this medication or using it for more than two weeks, laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., calcium, potassium, sodium, or bicarbonate levels) should be conducted. Ensure you attend all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. It is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
